text:
maya: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's transformer-engine flip (te.enable_fp8=true) we saw p50 jump ~20% on an H100 canary. attaching short traces and perf snippets.

liam: which kernel path is hot? fp8 TE path or some fallback path? any logs?

maya: mixed. matmuls pick fp8_te_gemm but attention falls back to an nvfuser int8 slowpath. logs show both: "selected kernel: fp8_te_gemm" then "attention: nvfuser_int8_attention_slowpath".

diego: can you paste the perf summary numbers?

maya: perf summary (small sample):
- baseline (fp16): p50=42ms p95=120ms
- fp8 experiment: p50=52ms p95=210ms
CPU-side attention overhead and queueing increased during the spike.

anjali: hmm KV cache hit-rate change? we've seen attention paths flip when the cache eviction pattern changes.

trent: saw something similar on L40S during long-context workloads (seq>=2048) — warmup spikes that settle after ~30s.

liam: is batching heuristic different for fp8 rollout? microbatch growth + kv replay could change occupancy and push attention into different kernel choice.

maya: profiler snippet I grabbed: 
```
kernel_select:
  matmul: fp8_te_gemm
  attention: nvfuser_attention_int8_slow
kv:
  hit_rate: 0.86 -> 0.62 during spike
```

diego: lower hit_rate means more recompute of full attention and more attention kernel invocations -> explains larger p95 tail.

anjali: quick mitigation idea: force attention to the TE attn kernel (te_attention_int8_fast) via runtime flag `--force-attn-te` and cap microbatch growth to 8.

maya: validated on canary: forcing TE attention + microbatch cap brings p50=44ms p95=128ms. quality delta on our calibration set: small degradation (BLEU-like -0.6).

trent: tradeoff confirmed: latency vs calibration. we need an eval-gated rollout rather than blind performance metric.

liam: suspect root cause: kernel occupancy estimator misestimates when sample distribution shifts (due to prefix caching + bursty microbatches), which with fp8 scales shifts changes cost model and triggers nvfuser fallback.

maya: I traced sampler: estimator uses recent seq_len histogram; with KV hits dropping we suddenly see more long sequences and the estimator picks the small-batch nvfuser attention path.

diego: actionable items I propose:
- bump kernel sampler rate on canaries from 1% -> 5% to collect more signals
- add a KV-hit-rate threshold guard to avoid switching kernels mid-spike
- rollout gate: auto-fallback if p95 > baseline*1.5 for 10m window

maya: opened PR for sampler rate change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521

anjali: I'll run the calibration eval harness on the forced-attn run and report quality diffs across prompt families.

trent: also notify eng-infra / SRE to check for thermal/clock changes on the H100 nodes — long bursts can change GPU clocks which interacts badly with occupancy assumptions.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed: runtime-canary / te-fp8-probe -> nodeset-h100-canary @ 10:21 UTC

liam: noted. please keep traces with selector logs and kv hit histograms.

maya: will attach full traces and a short flame chart to the PR. current short-term plan: keep forced-attn gate on canary for 4h, collect sampler data, then roll to 25% if eval looks ok. :thumbsup:

maya: last update: canary stable for ~3h with forced-attn + microbatch cap, p95 within target and sampler data looks promising. promoting to staggered rollout window tomorrow morning.
